newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc ends lower vs dollar but firm vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc ends lower vs dollar but firm vs mark.

text.p: 1610 GMT - The Swiss franc ended mixed, under pressure from the dollar but firmer versus the mark, as European traders generally moved in to sell marks on belief Germany will not raise interest rates any time soon.

"It really is entirely mark weakness," said one trader, noting that even against the Swiss franc "the mark has done rather poorly." He said that long-term interest rates in Germany were near or at historic lows, and markets saw no reason for the Bundesbank to raise short rates any time soon.
Weak growth in Germany and in Switzerland made it appear unlikely that there could be any tightening in those countries.
Swiss and German unemployment are at post-war highs.

Swiss Bank Corp's top economist said Tuesday he thought the Swiss National Bank (SNB) would shift its expansive monetary policy to a more neutral stance in the course of this year. But for now, few if any economists believe it will tighten, and some suggest it may even need to ease further.
Despite some indications after a meeting of the Group of Seven on Saturday that key countries see the dollar as strong enough, traders saw no real fear of intervention.
* Dollar ends at 1.4323/4328 Swiss francs on Tuesday, higher than 1.4260/4270 on Monday. * Mark ends at 85.73/76 Swiss centimes, lower than 86.23/26 centimes on Monday.
